facts.text: Architect Jose Luis Moreno built the original hotel without blueprints, using free-flowing designs sketched into the sand.
facts.excerpt: never using blueprints, he instead opted for free-flowing designs sketched into the sand

facts.text: Moreno began by building a restaurant between the jungle and sea, then added rooms and suites over the years for friends and family.
facts.excerpt: He fell in love with the Riviera Maya and built a restaurant between the jungle and sea. Over the years he would add rooms and suites to accommodate his friends and family

facts.text: Interior architect Tara Bernerd led the redesign, working with local artisans.
facts.excerpt: When approaching the redesign, interior architect Tara Bernerd sought to retain and enhance the natural beauty of the space

facts.text: All construction materials of the redesign (wood, stone, iron and ceramic) were sourced from Mexico.
facts.excerpt: All construction materials—the wood, stone, iron and ceramic—were sourced from Mexico.

facts.text: Casa Mayor echoes Moreno's original restaurant, with original features preserved.
facts.excerpt: Moreno’s original restaurant echoes through to today’s Casa Mayor, where original features are preserved and highlighted against colourful locally-woven fabrics.

facts.text: Woodend, a restaurant from Australian chef Curtis Stone, focuses on seafood cooked over an open flame.
facts.excerpt: Woodend, the new restaurant from Australian chef Curtis Stone, has a focus on exceptional seafood cooked over an open flame.

facts.text: Maroma Spa by Guerlain draws on the resort's history of Mayan wellness philosophy and offers sound and healing rituals.
facts.excerpt: Maroma Spa by Guerlain combines the resort’s history of Mayan wellness philosophy with Guerlain’s savoir-faire, infusing the pampering menu with new therapies including sound and healing rituals.

facts.text: The resort has Freddy's Bar and a second bar, Bambuco, described as a playful, vibrant Mexican space for sundowners.
facts.excerpt: Alongside long-time favourite Freddy’s Bar, Bambuco is another new bar that invites travellers into a playful, vibrant Mexican space for an unforgettable sundowner.

facts.text: Maroma works with Fundacion Selva Maya and Mayahuum to protect the endangered Melipona bee, the stingless bee sacred to the Mayan people.
facts.excerpt: Maroma is also continuing its work with local organisations Fundación Selva Maya and Mayahuum to protect the endangered Melipona bee, the stingless bee which was sacred to the Mayan people.

facts.text: Artwork throughout the resort has been sourced from Mexican artists.
facts.excerpt: Artwork throughout the resort has been sourced from Mexican artists

facts.text: The property sits on 200 acres of jungle, reached along a modest gravel road winding through mangroves off the main highway.
facts.excerpt: Winding through thick mangroves (the property sits on 200 acres of jungle) along a modest gravel road

facts.text: Maroma is thirty miles south of Cancun.
facts.excerpt: Thirty miles south of Cancun, Maroma first opened in 1995

facts.text: 80 percent of the property's furnishings and objects were made in Mexico.
facts.excerpt: 80 percent of the property’s furnishings and objects were made in Mexico

facts.text: The curved stucco buildings are aligned to Mayan geometry.
facts.excerpt: the curved stucco buildings are aligned to Mayan geometry

facts.text: Guests can take a tortilla-making class with chef Daniel Camacho.
facts.excerpt: The tortilla-making class that’s offered to guests, where Camacho will walk you through the three methods behind corn tortillas

facts.text: An excursion to a cenote about a 30-minute drive away is offered, with a guide from 4World Expeditions.
facts.excerpt: the excursion to a cenote about a 30-minute drive away

facts.text: Casa Mayor, from Mexican-born chef Daniel Camacho, uses ingredients from the Yucatan peninsula and is where breakfast is served.
facts.excerpt: Casa Mayor, a new spot from Mexican-born chef Daniel Camacho that incorporates a slew of ingredients from the Yucatán peninsula

facts.text: Each guest is checked in by a personal host, via iPad.
facts.excerpt: Once checked in (via iPad by your personal host)
